diagram_candidates.title: L=3 torus checks and syndrome calculation
diagram_candidates.claim: The example names all 18 horizontal and vertical edge qubits and 18 star/plaquette checks on the periodic 3×3 cellulation, then traces the horizontal primal loop h_(0,0), h_(1,0), h_(2,0) and the endpoint defects after each Z application.
diagram_candidates.concrete_content: Draw a 3×3 periodic square cellulation with distinct h_(i,j), v_(i,j) edge labels and q_(i,j), f_(i,j) vertices/faces, marking each A_(i,j) star on its four incident edges and each B_(i,j) plaquette on its four boundary edges. Highlight the h_(i,0) loop with arrows or numbered Z applications; show defects {q_(0,0),q_(1,0)}, then {q_(0,0),q_(2,0)}, then none after closure. Identify opposite boundaries as periodic, so the three-edge path closes on the torus.
diagram_candidates.uncertainty: Editorial candidate. The example already gives the exact incidence and syndrome calculation; a labeled cellulation would make periodic indexing and endpoint movement easier to scan.

diagram_candidates.title: Computational basis states have an extended stabilizer tableau
diagram_candidates.claim: For each bit position j, the basis state |x⟩ has stabilizer row s_(j+1)=(-1)^(x_j) Z_(j+1) and paired destabilizer row d_(j+1)=X_(j+1); the extended tableau condition is ω(d_(i+1),s_(j+1))=δ_(i,j), with zero pairings within either row family.
diagram_candidates.concrete_content: Show the 2n tableau rows in paired order, with columns for row role, phase k, X-label u, and Z-label v: s_(j+1) has k=2x_j, u=0, v=e_j; d_(j+1) has k=0, u=e_j, v=0. Include the pairing block matrix with zero diagonal-family blocks and identity cross-blocks, and label wires using the stated j↔j+1 indexing convention.
diagram_candidates.uncertainty: Editorial candidate. The formulas are already explicit; a small tableau makes the meaning of “extended tableau pairing conditions” and the phase/wire indexing more immediate.
